never_write.region: User DCSM OTP, zone 1 and zone 2 (link pointers, passwords, JTAGLOCK, CMAC key)
never_write.range: 0x78000-0x783FF (Z1 base 0x78000, Z2 base 0x78200); zone select blocks start at 0x78020
never_write.why: One-time programmable and ECC protected. A wrong ECC value blocks the device permanently. An all-0 password makes the zone permanently secure; an all-1 password loads as the BLOCKED state. TI pre-programs bits of every CSMPSWD1 word (Table 5-3), so a user may only flip 1 to 0 in the other bits.
never_write.source: SPRUIX1B sections 5.2.1, 5.2.6, 5.2.7, Table 5-3 and the CAUTION after Figure 5-2; SPRSP63B Table 7-2; driverlib hw_dcsm.h offsets

never_write.range: operations Z1/Z2 PasswordProgram, LINKPOINTERProgram, JTAGLOCKProgram, OTPSECLOCKProgram, JTAGPSWDH/LProgram, CMACKEYProgram, GPREGProgram, AllProgram, SecurityAutoFill, GRABEXEONLYProgram
never_write.why: Each one burns OTP bits. A frontend must never call them for a plain image write.

recovery.symptom: DSLite: Error -2131 'Unable to access device register' from IcePick_C_0
recovery.fix: Set property 'SWD Mode Settings' = 4 (cJTAG 2-pin) in the ccxml connection section, or start from C2000Ware's TMS320F2800137_LaunchPad.ccxml.

recovery.symptom: 'A firmware update is required for the XDS110 probe' then 'Timed out after 45 seconds'
recovery.fix: Update the probe with xdsdfu (ccs_base/common/uscif/xds110) to 3.0.0.43; DSLite has no Update button.

recovery.symptom: Flash operations fail with 'Flash registers are not writable. Please check whether the device is unsecured or not.'
recovery.fix: Zone is locked. Set Z1CSMPSWD0-3 / Z2CSMPSWD0-3 and run the Z1Unlock / Z2Unlock operation with the real password. A blank part unlocks itself: BOOTROM writes the default password into the KEY registers at start.

recovery.symptom: Zone password programmed as all zeros, or wrong ECC in User OTP
recovery.fix: None documented. TI states the zone is permanently secure, or the device must be replaced.
recovery.source: SPRUIX1B section 5.2.1 and CAUTION after Figure 5-2

recovery.symptom: JTAGLOCK enabled, no debug access
recovery.fix: Unlock with the 128-bit JTAG password through the CCStudio integrated tool; targetdb carries the 'JLM' (AJSM) subpath on port 0x13 with four unlock-key words.

recovery.symptom: 'Operation was aborted on C28xx_CPU1' on a low-power example
recovery.fix: Chip is asleep: press the wake button or reset, then reconnect.

write_paths.detail: DSLite (UniFlash 9.6.0 command line, 'dslite flash --config=<ccxml> [-s id=value] <image>') loads libFlashC2000F021 (partnum contains 'F2837') for this part (FlashDLLDB.xml). recovery.fix: Unlock-By-Scan through the AJSM tap, as on the R4 parts.

debug_port.access: ARM CS_DAP (port 16), no ICEPick; SWD is also available (JTAG-to-SWD switch sequences in the data sheet)
debug_port.notes: JTAG and SWD pins are PC0..PC3; they come up as JTAG at reset and can be reassigned to GPIO, which locks the debugger out (see recovery).

identify.field: 0x4BA00477 (OpenOCD stellaris.cfg also accepts 0x1BA00477 to 0x4BA00477 by ignoring the version nibble)
identify.source: TM4C123GH6PM data sheet JTAG chapter (IDCODE text); openocd target/stellaris.cfg

identify.field: DID0 CLASS bits 23:16 (0x05 = TM4C123x, 0x0A = TM4C129x); DID1 PARTNO bits 23:16
identify.source: TM4C123GH6PM and TM4C1294NCPDT data sheets; openocd stellaris.cfg reads 0x400fe000

write_paths.detail: DSLite loads libFlashStellaris (partnum begins 'TM4C', 'LM', 'TM4E'). Operations: Erase, BlankCheck, CalculateChecksum, ProgramUserRegister0/1, ReadUserRegister0/1, ProgramMACAddress, ReadMACAddress. Settings FlashEraseType (mass or by address range) and FlashEraseStartAddr/EndAddr. The LaunchPad kits use the ICDI connection (libicdi_emu.dylib ships for macOS).
write_paths.source: UniFlash 9.6.0 deskdb/content/TICloudAgent/osx/ccs_base/DebugServer/bin/FlashDLLDB.xml; libFlashStellaris.dylib strings; UniFlash 9.6.0 uniflash/public/target_setup/data/lpList.json

write_paths.detail: xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7 and TI's fork: 'flash bank ... stellaris' (autodetect), board files ti_ek-tm4c123gxl.cfg and ti_ek-tm4c1294xl.cfg with interface ti-icdi, transport jtag. Both binaries list TM4C123 (Blizzard) and TM4C129 (Snowflake) part names. Includes stellaris mass_erase and recover commands. Not run on our bench (no Tiva board).
write_paths.source: ~/zephyr-toolchain/xpack-openocd-0.12.0-7/openocd/scripts/target/stellaris.cfg, board/ti_ek-tm4c123gxl.cfg; strings of the openocd binaries

write_paths.detail: ROM Boot Loader (UART, and per device SSI, I2C, Ethernet, USB DFU) runs when flash word 0x00000004 is 0xFFFFFFFF, or when the BOOTCFG-selected GPIO matches. Documented in the TivaWare Boot Loader user's guide SPMU301; UniFlash has libFlashSerialStellaris for it.
write_paths.source: TM4C123GH6PM data sheet ROM and reset sections; FlashDLLDB.xml entries FlashSerialStellaris, FlashEthernetStellaris, FlashDFUStellaris

never_write.range: BOOTCFG (0x400FD1D0), FMPRE0-3 / FMPPE0-3 (0x400FD200 and 0x400FD400 ranges), USER_REG0-3
never_write.why: Committed once; not touched by erase or mass erase. BOOTCFG needs a power-on reset. A bad BOOTCFG or protection mask can lock the debug path; UniFlash's ProgramMACAddress operation writes USER_REG0/1.

recovery.symptom: Debugger cannot connect after the program reassigned the JTAG/SWD pins to GPIO, or the part is 'locked'
recovery.fix: Debug-port unlock sequence: hold RST, power up, do ten JTAG-to-SWD and SWD-to-JTAG switch sequences. This mass erases flash and the EEPROM and restores the non-volatile registers to factory defaults. OpenOCD's stellaris driver has a 'recover' command for it.
recovery.source: TM4C123GH6PM data sheet section 4.3.4.3; openocd strings stellaris_handle_recover_command

probe.launchpad: EK-TM4C123GXL, EK-TM4C1294XL, EK-TM4C129EXL: on-board ICDI (Stellaris ICDI, connection class 31040).
probe.bare_chip: Any JTAG or SWD probe on PC0 (TCK/SWCLK), PC1 (TMS/SWDIO), PC2 (TDI), PC3 (TDO).
